about: The plain words the kernel map (kernel-map.html, built by build_map.py) needs that the kernel's own files do not hold. Every name, count, layer, operation, state, class definition, tolerance and pin on the map is read from the repository: MAP.json (the crates and their layers), chapter 27's layer table, engine-geometry's generated/mcp-tools.json (what programs call), operations.json beside this file and the progress page's states (which engine answers each operation), chapter 9's exactness classes, and geom-solidcore's Cargo.toml and tests. This file adds only: (1) apps: the three uses of the kernel at the top of the map, in the order site, building, things that go in it, each with the plan file and text that names it, which the build checks are still there; (2) layers and crates: a few plain words for what each is for (every crate of MAP.json must have its line, and a line for a crate MAP.json does not list fails the build); (3) interface: the operation piece each family of the interface's operations belongs to; (4) classes: a plain gloss of each of chapter 9's classes, and the class of each operation our own core answers that the interface does not list yet, with where the repository says so; (5) engines: the words for the two engines, the class solidcore's answers have, and what each of its stored tolerances measures.

apps.note: All three are one program on one model; the plan calls Civil and Workshop its disciplines.

solidcore.for: An outside modelling engine for curved work, taken in whole
solidcore.why: Its answers are compared with ours on every stored case and must fall within the stated tolerances; that is measured, not proven.

tolerances.max_residual: every point of a meeting curve within {} of both surfaces
tolerances.length_relerr: the curve's length within {} of the true length, as a share of it
tolerances.volume_relerr_flat: a flat-faced volume within {} of the true volume, as a share of it
tolerances.volume_relerr_curved: a curved volume within {} of the true volume, as a share of it
tolerances.samples_per_piece: checked at {} points along each piece of curve
